subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Should OpenClaw retain queue-level neutralization of line-leading `System:` in externally influenced system-event text while removing the broader cosmetic bracket sanitizer?
rationale: The PR intentionally changes the product’s trust-text policy, but removing the queue protection conflicts with the renderer’s mechanical `System:`-per-line format. Maintainers need to choose the durable boundary rather than treating this as a cosmetic rename.

options.title: Keep narrow queue protection
options.body: Restore line-leading `System:` neutralization only at the system-event queue and keep the plain-label marker refactor elsewhere.

options.title: Redesign event rendering
options.body: Replace the line-oriented system-event encoding with a structured boundary that cannot be confused with event text, then prove all existing consumers preserve behavior.

options.title: Accept raw event text
options.body: Merge the removal and explicitly accept that queued external text may create additional system-looking prompt lines.

recommendation.title: Keep narrow queue protection
recommendation.body: Restore line-leading `System:` neutralization only at the system-event queue and keep the plain-label marker refactor elsewhere.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the adjacent model-bound prompt-context design and its trust-boundary rationale.
